prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Charlotte after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Charlotte for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I’ll put together a short, targeted list of specific Charlotte-area personal injury firms and why to call each — but I need one quick detail first:

- Do you want firms near a particular neighborhood or ZIP code in Charlotte? (Or is “anywhere in Charlotte” fine?)
- Any priorities: trial experience, quick settlements, firms that handle catastrophic injuries, Spanish or other language needs, low medical-lien/medical-pay assistance, or something else?

If you want the list right away, I can also give a recommended short call script and the exact questions to ask so you can compare firms quickly.

What I can give you now (immediately useful whether or not you share location):

1) One firm to call right away
- Morgan & Morgan (has a Charlotte office)
  - Why: large national plaintiff firm with lots of resources for medical bills, investigators and experts; handles serious car-accident cases and typically takes cases on contingency (no upfront attorney fee).
  - Good if you have significant injuries, multiple parties, or expect litigation.

2) How to build the rest of your short list
- Choose 3–5 firms: mix one large national/regional firm + 1–2 trusted local plaintiff firms + 1 experienced trial attorney (if you think case may go to court).
- Ask friends, check Google reviews, AVVO, Super Lawyers, and the North Carolina Bar directory for local plaintiffs’ attorneys.

3) What to ask when you call (short script + questions)
- Short script: “I was in a car accident on [date]. I need a personal injury attorney. Do you handle car-accident cases? Is there a free consultation? Will you take the case on contingency?”
- Key questions:
  - Do you handle car-accident personal injury claims in Mecklenburg County/Charlotte?
  - Who will work my case day-to-day (attorney or paralegal)?
  - What is your contingency fee and are there other costs I might need to pay up front or out of settlement?
  - Do you have trial experience with car-accident cases? (Ask for recent trial outcomes or verdicts.)
  - How do you handle medical bills/medical liens while the claim is pending?
  - Estimated timeline and likely next steps.
  - Can you provide references or recent client testimonials?
  - Do you communicate by phone/text/email and how often?

4) Red flags to avoid
- Pushy claims of “guaranteed” results or fixed settlement amounts without seeing records.
- Firms that won’t put fee structure in writing.
- Attorneys who won’t identify who will handle the case (ask for the attorney/associate name).
- Very low or no presence in local courts if your case may require litigation.

5) Immediate practical steps for you
- Get medical care and keep records/expenses.
- Preserve photos, police report number, witness contact info.
- Don’t sign any insurer release without talking to an attorney.
- Note how the other driver’s insurance handled the claim and their policy info if available.

If you want that specific list of 5–7 Charlotte firms (names, phone numbers, and why each is a good fit), tell me your ZIP code and what matters most to you (trial experience, bilingual, catastrophic injury, quick settlement, etc.) and I’ll compile it now.
